tasks.title: First occurrence: naive search
tasks.statement: Write a function find_first(text, pat): the index of the first occurrence of the pattern pat in the string text, or -1 if there is none. An empty pattern occurs at position 0. Solve it with two nested loops: the shift and the character-by-character comparison, without find, index and in.
tasks.hint: For each shift i, compare text[i + j] and pat[j] while the characters are equal; if you reach the pattern length, you have found it.

tasks.title: Common beginning of words
tasks.statement: Write a function common_prefix(words): the longest common beginning of all words in the list. For an empty list, or if there is no common beginning, return an empty string.
tasks.hint: Take the first word as the pattern and shorten the length of the common beginning with each following word.

tasks.title: How many times it occurs, including overlaps
tasks.statement: Write a function count_overlapping(text, pat): the number of occurrences of the pattern pat (it is non-empty) in text, where occurrences may overlap: in «aaaa» the pattern «aa» occurs three times.
tasks.hint: After each occurrence found, move forward by just one position, not by the pattern length.

tasks.title: Prefix function
tasks.statement: Write a function prefix_function(s): a list p of the same length, where p[i] is the length of the longest proper prefix of the substring s[0..i] that equals its suffix. For «abacaba» the answer is [0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 2, 3]. The time is linear.
tasks.hint: Keep k, the current match length; on a mismatch, roll back: k = p[k - 1].

tasks.title: Longest border
tasks.statement: A border of a string is a proper prefix that equals a suffix. Write a function longest_border(s): the longest border as a string (empty if there are no borders). For «abacaba» it is «aba».
tasks.hint: The last value of the prefix function is the length of the longest border.

tasks.title: Smallest period
tasks.statement: Write a function min_period(s): the smallest length p such that the whole string consists of repetitions of its first p characters (p divides the length). If there is no such p smaller than the length, the answer is the length of the string; for an empty string it is 0. For example, for «abcabcabc» the answer is 3, and for «abcab» it is 5.
tasks.hint: The candidate period is the length minus the last prefix function value; check that it divides the length.

tasks.title: Knuth–Morris–Pratt search
tasks.statement: Write a function find_all(text, pat): a list of the starting positions of all occurrences of the pattern in the text (with overlaps), in increasing order. An empty pattern occurs at every position from 0 to len(text). The time is on the order of n + m: the check feeds in a text of a million characters and a pattern of three hundred thousand. The following are forbidden: find, index, count, startswith, split, replace, in and re.
tasks.hint: Build the prefix function of the pattern, then walk along the text: the text pointer never goes back, and k rolls back along the table.

tasks.title: How many times each prefix occurs
tasks.statement: Write a function prefix_occurrences(s): a list ans, where ans[l - 1] is how many times the prefix of length l occurs in s as a substring (with overlaps). For «abab» the answer is [2, 2, 1, 1]. The time is linear.
tasks.hint: Each prefix function value is an occurrence of a prefix of that length; then push the counters along the chain p[l - 1].

tasks.title: Cyclic shift
tasks.statement: Write a function is_rotation(a, b): whether b can be obtained from a by a cyclic shift. The time is linear: the check feeds in strings of five hundred thousand characters. The following are forbidden: slices, find, index, count, startswith, split, replace, in and re.
tasks.hint: b is a shift of a if b occurs in the concatenation a + a; search for it with the prefix function, without creating extra copies.

tasks.title: Shortest palindrome by prepending
tasks.statement: Write a function shortest_palindrome(s): prepend to s on the left the minimum number of characters so that the result is a palindrome, and return it. For «abcd» the answer is «dcbabcd». The time is linear: the check feeds in a string of four hundred thousand characters. The following are forbidden: find, index, count, startswith, split, replace, in and re.
tasks.hint: Find the longest palindromic prefix: the prefix function of s + separator + reversed s.

tasks.title: Z-function
tasks.statement: Write a function z_function(s): a list z, where z[i] is the length of the longest common beginning of the string s and its suffix starting at position i. We take z[0] to be 0. For «aabxaab» the answer is [0, 1, 0, 0, 3, 1, 0]. The time is linear.
tasks.hint: Keep the Z-block [l, r): inside it start with min(r − i, z[i − l]), then extend character by character.

tasks.title: Search with the Z-function
tasks.statement: Write a function z_count(text, pat): the number of occurrences of a non-empty pattern in the text (with overlaps), using the Z-function of the concatenation pat + separator + text. The time is linear: the check feeds in a text of a million characters. The following are forbidden: find, index, count, startswith, split, replace, in and re.
tasks.hint: z[i] == len(pat) at a position i > len(pat) means an occurrence; the separator keeps z from growing beyond the pattern length.

tasks.title: Substring hash in constant time
tasks.statement: Write a class SubHash: the constructor SubHash(s) computes the prefix hashes; the method get(l, r) returns the hash of the substring s[l:r] in O(1), and the method same(l1, l2, length) returns True if the substrings s[l1:l1+length] and s[l2:l2+length] are equal (compared by hashes, without slices). Use a large modulus, for example 2^61 − 1. The check: a string of nine hundred thousand characters and two hundred thousand queries. The following are forbidden: slices, find, index, count, startswith, split, replace, in and re.
tasks.hint: H[i + 1] = (H[i] · B + character code) mod M; the hash of [l, r) = H[r] − H[l] · B^(r − l) mod M.

tasks.title: Rabin–Karp algorithm
tasks.statement: Write a function rabin_karp(text, pat): the index of the first occurrence of pat in text, or -1; for an empty pattern it is 0. Compute the pattern hash and a rolling window hash (a large modulus, for example 2^61 − 1), and when the hashes are equal, compare the strings. The check: a text of a million characters and a pattern of three hundred thousand. The following are forbidden: slices, find, index, count, startswith, split, replace, in and re.
tasks.hint: The window: ht = ((ht − code of the departed character · B^(m−1)) · B + code of the new one) mod M; do not forget to take the remainder after the subtraction.

tasks.title: Prefix tree
tasks.statement: Write a class Trie with the methods insert(word), contains(word) → bool and count_prefix(prefix) → how many distinct inserted words start with prefix (an empty prefix means all words). Inserting a word again changes nothing. The check: a hundred thousand words and a hundred thousand queries, so scanning a list will not be fast enough.
tasks.hint: In each node store a dictionary of children, an end-of-word flag and how many words pass through the node.

tasks.title: Autocomplete
tasks.statement: Write a function autocomplete(words, prefix, k): the first k words (without repeats) from the list words that start with prefix, in alphabetical order. If there are fewer than k such words, return as many as there are.
tasks.hint: Descend into the trie along the prefix and traverse the subtree, visiting children in alphabetical order, until you collect k words.

tasks.title: Levenshtein distance
tasks.statement: Write a function edit_distance(a, b): the minimum number of insertions, deletions and substitutions of a character that turn a into b. For «kitten» and «sitting» the answer is 3. The time is on the order of len(a) · len(b).
tasks.hint: d[i][j] = d[i − 1][j − 1] if the characters are equal; otherwise 1 + the minimum of the three neighbors. Two table rows are enough.

tasks.title: One edit
tasks.statement: Write a function one_edit_away(a, b): True if a can be turned into b by at most one insertion, deletion or substitution of a character (equal strings also give True). The time is linear, without a table.
tasks.hint: Find the first position where the strings differ and check the remaining tails for the three length cases.

tasks.title: Longest common subsequence
tasks.statement: Write a function lcs_length(a, b): the length of the longest common subsequence of two strings, where the characters go in the same order but not necessarily consecutively. For «abcde» and «ace» the answer is 3.
tasks.hint: If the last characters match, the length is one more than for the prefixes; otherwise take the maximum of «without the last one in a» and «without the last one in b».

tasks.title: How many distinct substrings
tasks.statement: Write a function count_distinct(s): the number of distinct non-empty substrings of the string s. For «aaa» the answer is 3, and for «abab» it is 7. You cannot store all the substrings: the check feeds in strings of two thousand characters, and the sandbox memory is limited. The idea: when a character is appended to a prefix of length i, new substrings appear, namely the suffixes that did not occur before. Their number is i minus the largest prefix function value of the reversed prefix.
tasks.hint: The new substrings when appending a character are the suffixes that have not occurred before; their count is i minus the maximum π of the reversed prefix.
